project_context.tagline: The only heritage Mithila brand in Kathmandu
project_context.aesthetic: Warm, earthy, heritage/artisanal. Never dark or moody. Award-worthy 3D aesthetic.

headings.usage: H1, H2, H3, large manifesto numbers, editorial marquee.
headings.guidelines: Use fluid typography sizes (e.g., clamp). Very tight tracking for large headings. Never use standard sans-serif for headings.

body.usage: Paragraphs, UI elements, small tags, CTA buttons.
body.guidelines: Loose line-height (leading-relaxed) for readability. Moderate tracking.

visual_enhancers.textures: Madhubani folk-art line work (sun face, peacock, lotus, tree of life, triangle border). Use as extremely subtle SVG overlays or borders with opacity 10-20% in Deep Maroon or Kraft Brown.
visual_enhancers.shapes: Clipped frames (e.g., archways, pill shapes) for images. No harsh 90-degree corners on feature imagery.
visual_enhancers.depth: Implement a 2.5D parallax depth effect using staggered layers, large soft drop shadows (warm tinted, e.g., rgba(74, 31, 13, 0.1)), and blurred background elements.
visual_enhancers.glassmorphism: Warm glassmorphism. Avoid cold icy glass. Use `bg-creamLight/60 backdrop-blur-xl border-white/20`.

layouts.general: Mobile-first responsive. Avoid standard Bootstrap grids. Use 'The Swiss Grid' mixed with 'The Bento Grid' for asymmetry.
layouts.spacing: Extremely generous padding (`py-24` to `py-32` between sections).
layouts.alignment: Optical alignment. Left-align text blocks, but feel free to stagger elements across the grid.

grids.bento: Asymmetrical, e.g., grid-cols-12 where elements span 4, 8, or 6 columns overlapping.

motion.choreography: Smooth momentum scrolling (lenis). Elements enter via staggered fade-ins and subtle upward translations. Hero text uses line-by-line masked reveals. Parallax on images.
motion.3d_aesthetic: Use framer-motion `useScroll` and `useTransform` to move foreground image layers faster than background ones. Add subtle 3D tilt on product cards using `framer-motion`.

accessibility.contrast: Ensure minimum 4.5:1 ratio for standard text. Test Dark Ink against Cream Light.
accessibility.testing: All interactive elements MUST include a `data-testid` attribute (kebab-case, role-based).

media.image_treatment: Spotlight effect, warm lighting, masked/clipped frames (archways). Images should never feel 'dropped in'—they must feel integrated into the page geometry.

steps: 1. Instead of heavy WebGL/Three.js, achieve the requested '3D aesthetic' by using 2.5D layering with framer-motion.
2. Separate hero images into foreground (product), midground (text), and background (texture/color).
3. Use `useScroll` from framer-motion to track scroll progress.
4. Apply `useTransform` to shift the foreground on the Y-axis at a 1.5x speed multiplier, midground at 1.0x, and background at 0.5x.
5. Apply a 3D tilt effect on hover for product cards (`rotateX`, `rotateY` mapped to mouse position).

component_path.guidelines: Use standard HTML/Tailwind for marketing layout structures. DO NOT use rigid Shadcn cards for the main marketing sections, only for complex UI (e.g. Accordion/FAQ).

instructions_to_main_agent: Build as a single-page scrolling website (.js, React).
Use Framer Motion heavily for the cinematic scrolling, 3D tilt effects, and text reveals.
Implement Lenis for smooth momentum scrolling at the App root.
Ensure all fonts and exactly the provided hex colors are used.
Generate necessary Madhubani SVG patterns (sun face, tree of life) inline or use CSS patterns mimicking them.
Maintain the warm, earthy aesthetic—do not let the design slip into generic dark-mode or standard SaaS styles.
UNIVERSAL_GUIDELINES_FOR_MAIN_AGENT: Do not use generic centered layouts or simplistic gradients.
Create depth through layered design elements with z-index hierarchy.
Use framer-motion `useScroll` and `useTransform` to create a 2.5D parallax effect.
DO NOT use pure transparent backgrounds for text-overlays. Use warm glassmorphism.
All interactive elements MUST have `data-testid` attributes (kebab-case).
Ensure generous spacing (`py-24` or `py-32`) for an editorial, cinematic feel.
